title: 2  Municipal Overview
text:
2.1 Progress to Date
The Town of Amherst Municipality was responsible for 4487.6 Metric Tons of CO2 Equivalent emissions in FY 2016. In FY 2025, this number was 3731.9. This represents a 16.8% decrease in municipal emissions relative to the 2016 baseline, which failed to meet the Town’s 25% emissions reduction goal for 2025. To meet the 2030 goal, the Town would need to reach 2,244 MTCO2e emissions, which represents a near 40% decrease in current emissions over the span of 5 years.

title: 3  Municipal Stationary Energy
text:
3.1 Buildings
Stationary emissions accounted for 3,195 MTCO2e in 2016, and 2,704 MTCO2e in 2025, representing a 15.4% reduction. Notably, despite an overall reduction in municipal emissions since 2022, stationary energy emissions were slightly higher in 2025 than they were in 2022, an increase of 78 MTCO2e.
The 10 municipal buildings with the highest emissions account for 2234.7 MTCO2e in 2025, which accounts for 61% of total municipal emissions.

title: 2  Municipal Overview
text:
2.2 Emissions by Sector
Municipal emissions fall into two categories: stationary energy and transportation. Stationary energy accounted for 73.9% of total emissions in 2025, up from 68.6% in 2022. As it has been reported, electricity usage from electric vehicles (EVs) has been absorbed into stationary energy, so this increase in electricity consumption may reflect the increased adoption of EVs and their miscategorization as stationary energy, rather than a simple reduction in transportation emissions.








Figure 2.2: Municipal GHG emissions (MTCO2e) by reporting year, excluding transmission and distribution losses

title: 2  Municipal Overview
text:
2.3 Emissions by Fuel Type
As shown in Figure 2.3, the composition of fuel usage has changed over time within the municipality. Most notably, electricity has seen an increased share of total emissions, from 36% in 2022 to 46% in 2025, while the relative shares of gasoline and diesel have decreased. This is consistent with the Town’s move toward more renewable energy sources.

title: Greenhouse Gas Inventory FY 2025
text:
1.1 Background
The Town of Amherst Massachusetts seeks to achieve net zero community emissions by 2050, an ambitious goal set by the Town’s Energy and Climate Action Committee (ECAC) in their 2021 Climate Action, Adaptation, and Resilience Plan (CAARP). Using the 2016 emissions inventory as a baseline, the intermediary goals of 25% reduction in emissions by 2025 and 50% reduction in emissions by 2030 were set as well.
To accurately assess progress toward the ultimate goal of carbon neutrality, periodic emissions inventories are essential for tracking emissions trends and evaluating the effectiveness of climate action initiatives. This report seeks to determine whether the Town has achieved their 2025 target, to evaluate progress toward future milestones, to identify areas of success, and to identify areas that require further intervention.

text:

The Town has made significant progress toward achieving its 2025 emissions reduction target. There are numbers that exist to support this, but I have not finalized them, so this paragraph is really just a placeholder so I can get a sense of how things look before I get the aforementioned numbers.
